what: The fluid each locomotion mode happens in, with the two properties the Reynolds number needs. Nothing here is about any organism: these are properties of water and air at a stated temperature.
why_it_is_a_file: A Reynolds number is only as good as the viscosity behind it, and a viscosity written inline in a check is a number nobody can argue with. These are standard reference values at a stated temperature, which is NOT the same as a measurement of the fluid the organism is actually in: a bacterium in mucus, in biofilm, or in cytoplasm is in something very much more viscous than water, and the check says so rather than pretending 20 C water covers it.

water.label: fresh water at 20 C
water.source: standard reference values for pure water at 20 C and 1 atm (CRC Handbook of Chemistry and Physics, fluid properties tables)
water.caveat: Pure water at 20 C. Culture medium, pond water, mucus, biofilm and cytoplasm are all more viscous, some by orders of magnitude, and a Reynolds number computed with this value is an UPPER bound on the real one for a swimmer in any of them.

seawater.label: seawater at 20 C, 35 PSU
seawater.source: standard reference values for seawater at 20 C, salinity 35 PSU, 1 atm (oceanographic property tables)
seawater.caveat: Varies with temperature and salinity; polar seawater is roughly twice as viscous as this.

air.label: air at 15 C, sea level (ISA)
air.source: International Standard Atmosphere, sea level, 15 C, 101.325 kPa
air.caveat: Density falls with altitude. A flier at 3000 m has about 74 % of this density and a correspondingly higher minimum airspeed.

regimes.what: Where the boundaries of the Reynolds regimes are put, and why that is a convention and not a fact.
regimes.note: There is no sharp boundary. Re = 1 is the conventional marker for where viscous forces dominate inertial ones and Re ~ 1000 for where inertia dominates; between them both matter and neither limit applies. The scallop theorem is a statement about the STOKES limit (Re -> 0), and applying it at Re = 0.9 rather than Re = 0.001 is a judgement, so the check reports the number and says how far into the limit the design actually is.
